header: FRONT-PATH RULE (step 38c): who owns a question when the structured data cannot answer it. THE PROBLEM (seen 18 Oct on "which pathology room should non-executive employees report to for the health check-up in January 2026"): the SQL engine answers an employee or health check-up question from its views. When it says "unanswerable" (the views hold no room column), the route used to return that message as the FINAL answer, so the circular search, which may well hold the room, never ran. MY RULE: an "unanswerable" answer is final only when the question points at one particular person, department or ticket (a salary of a named person is NOT in any circular: say so). When nobody is named, I let the circulars have their turn first; the route keeps the engine's explanation and shows it only if the circulars have nothing either. Anything the rule cannot judge (the directory's name list is unavailable, a non-Latin question) keeps today's behaviour: the explanation is final. This is pure except for the loader it is handed. Unit-tested by dataGapRule.selftest.ts.

symbols.name: EnginePayload
doc: The part of the SQL engine's payload this rule reads (a structural type, because the engine's module is heavy).

symbols.sig: export async function continueToCirculars( payload: EnginePayload | null | undefined, q: string, loadDirectoryWords: () => Promise<ReadonlySet<string>>, ctx: { isNameShaped: boolean; deptMentioned: boolean },): Promise<boolean>
doc: True when the circulars should be tried before I return the engine's "unanswerable" explanation as final.

symbols.name: INTERNAL
doc: A model explanation that names the database's own parts ("The health_checkups view does not include a pathology-room column") means nothing to a reader, so I detect it here.

symbols.name: PLAIN_DATA_GAP
symbols.sig: const PLAIN_DATA_GAP = "The directory and the health check-up schedules do not hold that information."

symbols.name: CONTACT_DATA
doc: WHEN THE REASON IS THAT CONTACT DATA IS WITHHELD. The language model that writes the database questions is never given phone numbers, e-mail or home addresses, only yes/no flags (src/lib/nl2sql/sql/01_nlq_schema_views_role.sql: "can COUNT people without email but can never READ an address"). A question that needs the digits or the letters (a number that starts with ..., an address that contains ...) is therefore refused by the model, and the plain "the directory does not hold that information" that used to replace its explanation was untrue: the directory holds them and keeps them out of reach on purpose. So I say that, and I say where a number can be seen.

symbols.name: CONTACT_WITHHELD
symbols.sig: const CONTACT_WITHHELD = "Phone numbers, e-mail and home addresses are kept out of reach of this search on purpose, so it cannot look inside them …

symbols.name: friendlyUnanswerable
doc: Returns the explanation as shown: the model's own words, unless they name the database's internals; and when the reason is withheld contact data, I give the true reason in plain words.

behaviours: THE CASE: the pathology room question goes on to the circulars
a question about a rule or a place with people-data words goes on
a general question the data cannot answer goes on
a salary of a NAMED person stays final (the directory word 'sanjay')
a ticket number stays final
a person's name as the whole question stays final
a department stays final
a plural surname ('mazumdars') counts as a person
a clarifying question is never sent on
an answer is never sent on
no payload: nothing to continue
the directory's name list unavailable: final
an empty name list: final
a Hindi question is not judged: final
an empty question is final
namesSomeone: a directory word
namesSomeone: a ticket-like number
namesSomeone: the people-data words alone do not name anyone
namesSomeone: a year is not a ticket
directoryWordIn: finds a plural by its singular and reports the word as typed
a plain explanation is kept
a message naming the view and the column is replaced
a message with 'nlq.employees' is replaced
a refusal because phone numbers are withheld says so, in plain words, whether or not it names the database's parts
that sentence tells the truth (kept out on purpose, not 'does not hold'), and says where a number can be seen: by name or ticket, masked, with Reveal
other missing data (salary, a pathology room) still gets the old plain sentence
an empty message becomes the plain one
a message with 'table' in ordinary words is replaced too (a reader does not need it)
